answer: Each identity anchors one basalt block and locks 80 credits. A saffron seal keyed to that identity is cast into the block. At each high tide the anchor must hold a 200-kilogram pull, and the auditor recomputes pull, seal, and weight. Reusing a block or seal fails and burns both bonds. So each fake needs a new block, seal, and tide test: 45 casting plus 25 test plus 80 locked, 150 in all. The kth fake pays 150, so 1,000 fakes cost 150,000. A rented-anchor ring fails because a seal keyed to one identity cannot pass a pull. An honest operator anchors once and recovers the 80 after a tide cycle.
